newsitem.title: GERMANY: At least one man held hostage in German bank.
newsitem.headline: At least one man held hostage in German bank.

text.p: An armed robber took at least one person hostage in a Munich bank on Thursday, German police said.
A police spokesman said the man had entered the bank in the southern city's Grosshadern district at around 8.30 a.m local time (0730 GMT) and was holding the hostage inside the building.
One man was being held captive and it was unclear if there were other hostages, police said. They were also unsure if the hostage-taker was acting alone.
Police sealed off the area shortly after the incident began. It came almost exactly a year after Munich police had to deal with two hostage dramas within 24 hours.
They first stormed a bank where an armed man was holding three people hostage for a ransom of four million marks ($2.8 million). All the captives and the hostage-taker were unharmed.
Hours later they shot dead a man who threatened to kill his girlfriend and a policeman. The man fired at police after they came to investigate a domestic row .
He then grabbed an officer who tried to stop him fleeing and held him captive for half an hour.
Police also shot dead a man who held 12 people in a dental surgery in the nearby town of Dachau in February.
